content.mission: Adaptive Dynamic Queue Scheduling and Cost-Aware Repair Orchestration
content.scientificQuestion: Can governed repair work be scheduled dynamically according to expected structural complexity and verification cost without weakening any existing security or verification boundary?

hypotheses.H1_CostAwareScheduling: Cost-aware scheduling reduces aggregate execution + verification cost vs FIFO.
hypotheses.H2_ComplexityAwareScheduling: Complexity-aware ordering reduces mean queue waiting time under heterogeneous workloads.
hypotheses.H3_ReviewPolicyInvariance: Scheduling MUST NOT override Phase 81's selective-review escalation policy.
hypotheses.H4_PriorityNotAuthority: High-priority items cannot bypass policy, review, gates, or verification.
hypotheses.H5_SchedulerDeterminism: Identical queue state produces byte-identical scheduling decisions.
hypotheses.H6_AntiStarvation: Repeatedly expensive workflows are never permanently starved.
hypotheses.H7_StaleWorkSuppression: Workflows with stale source revision are rejected before execution.
hypotheses.H8_BoundedOptimizationGain: Empirical measurement of actual queue optimization gain.
